Subject: NeuraHealth trial: prompt batch handover + success metrics roadmap

Thanks again for the call today — great alignment on the pilot scope. This thread is a short recap and proposed next steps to get the prompt/log handoff and evaluation plan moving.

Key outcomes from our call:
- Pilot goal: Validate that Redwood can meet 95th percentile latency <300ms and maintain answer relevance >= 88% on your priority prompt set for triage suggestions.
- Data we need from NeuraHealth: 1) representative prompt batch (~2k prompts across channels), 2) 100 anonymized triage logs (include timestamps & outcome labels), 3) example edge-case prompts.
- Timeline: initial handoff by Aug 1; Redwood will run an ingestion + baseline eval in 5 business days; alignment review on Aug 9.
- Success metrics (draft): precision@1 for top suggestion, latency P95, token cost per 1k requests, regression rate against baseline prompt set.

Action items (owners):
1) Evan: upload prompt batch + logs to the shared Drive folder (see link below) by 2028-08-01. Mark which prompts are high-priority. (owner: Evan)
2) Priya: define eval rubric and provide POC_Success_Metrics_Template.xlsx. (owner: Priya)
3) Karthik: run baseline ingestion/quality checks, produce initial eval report within 5 business days of receipt. (owner: Karthik)
4) Marissa: coordinate CS check-in and ensure any redaction/PII notes are captured. (owner: Marissa)
5) Lydia: confirm any compliance constraints for logs (retention, redaction).

Attachments included for upload/initial templates: neura_prompt_samples_v1.json (sample format), POC_Success_Metrics_Template.xlsx, POC_SLA_Draft.pdf (SLA + data handling).

Shared folder (for upload): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1N3-ExampleDriveLink
HubSpot record: HS-54821

Next steps: Evan to upload by Aug 1 -> Karthik begins ingestion -> sync review Aug 9. If any of these dates are tight, flag here and we'll adjust.

Thanks,

Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Priya — that captures the call well. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt batch: we'll deliver 2,400 prompts (mix of web, chat, and intake forms). We'll tag each with channel and priority. Is JSONL or JSON better?
2) Logs: 100 logs are fine but we need confirmation on redaction standards you require. We can strip PHI, but need to know if tokenization or pseudonymization is preferred.

We plan to upload the files to the Drive link by 2028-07-31 to leave a day buffer. Also attaching a short sample of our prompt schema in this reply (see: neura_sample_schema.json stub).

Best,
Evan

Subject: Re: NeuraHealth trial: prompt batch handover + success metrics roadmap

Evan — JSONL is ideal for the prompt batch (one prompt per line) but we can accept a JSON array as well. For the logs please apply the following minimal redaction checklist: 

- Remove direct identifiers (names, SSNs, exact addresses).
- Replace patient identifiers with stable pseudonyms if you want consistent tracking across logs.
- Keep timestamps and outcome labels.
- If unsure, send a small redaction sample and Marissa will confirm.

I'll attach the POC_Success_Metrics_Template.xlsx to this thread so you can see the fields we'll populate (we included example thresholds aligned to our runtime profiles). Karthik — once files land, can you run the initial schema check + tokenization cost estimate and confirm you have the right compute profile? Preferably run on the g4dn-equivalent baseline we discussed.

If NeuraHealth wants, we can also run an A/B with a quantized model variant to show cost/latency tradeoffs; we'll note that in the eval plan.

Thanks — looking forward to the upload.

Priya
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
